question: An engineer must integrate Cisco ACI with a VMware vSphere environment. The requirement is to use a VMware Distributed Virtual Switch and to assign the encapsulation VLAN of the EPG from the VLAN pool. Which configuration set accomplishes this goal?
options: Create a VMM domain association under the EPGs. Create a VLAN pool with static allocated VLANs.
Create a physical domain association under the EPGs. Create a VLAN pool with dynamic allocated VLANs.
Create a physical domain association under the EPGs. Create a VLAN pool with static allocated VLANs.
Create a VMM domain association under the EPGs. Create a VLAN pool with dynamic allocated VLANs.
theory: Integrating ACI with VMware vSphere through a Distributed Virtual Switch requires a VMM domain association on the EPG, which is what lets APIC push port-group configuration into vCenter and dynamically assign VLAN encapsulation as EPGs are consumed by VMs. A dynamically allocated VLAN pool is required, rather than static, because APIC itself automatically picks and assigns VLAN IDs from the pool as EPGs are deployed to the VMM domain — the defining behavior of a dynamic pool versus a statically pre-assigned one, which is typically paired with physical domains instead. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — ACI VMM Domain Integration and Dynamic VLAN Pools)
